targets.authors: Fleeson, W., Malanos, A. B., & Achille, N. M.
targets.title: An intraindividual process approach to the relationship between extraversion and positive affect: Is acting extraverted as “good” as being extraverted?
targets.evidence_quote: We predicted that Fleeson et al.’s (2002) core findings would replicate. That is, our participants would be able to act as we instructed them, and acting extraverted would cause positive affect, regardless of disposition.
targets.outcome_quote: In sum, this study replicates the finding that, regardless of underlying trait disposition, extraverted behavior produces greater positive affect than introverted behavior.
targets.outcome_reasoning: The reported positive-affect benefit and/or absence of dispositional negative-affect cost agrees with this original’s findings. Cognitive depletion is a novel extension, not a failed replication of these mood findings.

targets.title: The causal effects of extraversion on positive affect and neuroticism on negative affect: Manipulating state extraversion and state neuroticism in an experimental approach.
targets.evidence_quote: Although possible, two studies have assessed negative affect under similar circumstances and have failed to find the state by trait interaction that would suggest a mood cost for acting counterdispositionally (McNiel & Fleeson, 2006; McNiel et al., 2010). Therefore, our studies include between-subjects manipulations, larger sample sizes, and measures of both positive and negative affect to better assess any possible distress that might accompany counterdispositional behavior.
targets.outcome_quote: This study tested whether the pattern of relationships among extraversion, mood, behavior, and cognition found in Study 1 would generalize to a new interview situation. Very similar to previous research, participants reported more positive affect when acting extraverted, and this did not depend on their dispositional levels of extraversion. We again tested whether acting counterdispositionally might cause negative affect (along with positive affect in the case of introverts) and again failed to find any evidence for this idea.
targets.outcome_reasoning: The reported positive-affect benefit and/or absence of dispositional negative-affect cost agrees with this original’s findings. Cognitive depletion is a novel extension, not a failed replication of these mood findings.
